selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is this part of the book called?
questions.answer: The Twenty-First Word.

questions.question: Who are the prayers required for in the verse?
questions.answer: Believers.

questions.question: What did the man say was good, even though he still complained?
questions.answer: He said the prayers were good.

questions.question: What happened when the speaker paid attention to his inner self?
questions.answer: He heard the same complaint there.

questions.question: What feeling did he have about repeating prayer every day?
questions.answer: He felt worn out by it.

questions.question: What did he discover in his own nafs?
questions.answer: The same complaint.

questions.question: Why did the speaker decide to begin with himself?
questions.answer: Because a person should fix his own nafs before trying to fix others.

questions.question: What was the speaker’s first step before helping other people?
questions.answer: Reforming his own inner self.

questions.question: Why did he not start by blaming other people?
questions.answer: He knew he needed to correct himself first.

questions.question: What words come at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: Saying Allah’s name and asking His mercy and compassion.

questions.question: What message does the verse give about the timing of salah?
questions.answer: Salah has appointed times.

questions.question: What mistake did the man make about the prayers?
questions.answer: He treated them like a burden instead of a regular duty.

questions.question: Who first said praying five times was too much?
questions.answer: A man who was older and important.

questions.question: Did the speaker ignore that complaint or test it in himself?
questions.answer: He tested it in himself.

questions.question: From whom was the nafs taking that wrong idea?
questions.answer: From Satan.

questions.question: Why can’t someone guide others well before fixing himself?
questions.answer: Because he must work on his own wrong side first.

questions.question: What wise choice did the speaker make?
questions.answer: He chose to work on himself first.

questions.question: After understanding this, what did he say he would do?
questions.answer: Start with his own nafs.

questions.question: What is the title of the section after the opening lines?
questions.answer: First Station.

questions.question: According to the verse, are prayers random or ordered?
questions.answer: They are ordered at fixed times.

questions.question: What does the opening verse teach about prayer times?
questions.answer: They are set by Allah for believers.

questions.question: What kind of complaint did the man make about praying five times a day?
questions.answer: He said it felt too frequent and exhausting.

questions.question: What bad thing was helping the nafs think that way?
questions.answer: Laziness.

questions.question: What kind of nafs did he say he had?
questions.answer: A nafs that pushes toward wrong.
